title: Custom Kubernetes Operator in Go with CRD Lifecycle Reconciler, Automated Failover & Backup Controller
problem: Running stateful distributed applications on Kubernetes using standard StatefulSets leads to uncoordinated leader elections, unmonitored replication lag, and manual, error-prone disaster recovery. Generic controllers lack application-specific operational knowledge required for safe failover and automated point-in-time snapshots. This project builds a production-grade Kubernetes Operator in Go using the controller-runtime framework. The operator defines custom resource definitions (CRDs) for stateful database clusters, executes declarative reconciliation loops managing primary-replica topologies, performs automated health checks with split-brain prevention, and orchestrates zero-downtime rolling upgrades and scheduled cloud storage backups.

use_cases.title: Self-Service Internal Database Platform for Engineering Teams
use_cases.first_sentence: Enterprise platform engineering teams need to provide software developers with self-service, highly available database clusters without ticketing delays.
use_cases.second_sentence: Developers declare desired database topology in simple YAML manifests, and the operator automatically provisions StatefulSets, Services, and replication secrets.

use_cases.title: Automated Primary Node Failover & Disaster Recovery
use_cases.first_sentence: Site reliability engineers require automated remediation when a database primary node suffers hardware failure or network isolation.
use_cases.second_sentence: The operator detects primary unresponsiveness within 10 seconds, selects the most up-to-date replica, promotes it to primary, and reconfigures downstream nodes.

use_cases.title: Zero-Downtime Rolling Database Engine Upgrades
use_cases.first_sentence: Database administrators need to apply security patches and minor version engine upgrades across hundreds of production instances without service interruption.
use_cases.second_sentence: The operator coordinates an ordered rolling update, upgrading replicas first before executing a controlled switchover of the primary node.

hard_parts: Implementing idempotent reconciliation loops with controller-runtime that handle out-of-order Kubernetes API events
Preventing split-brain scenarios during network partitions through distributed quorum checks and fencing mechanisms
Orchestrating safe rolling updates on stateful workloads without data corruption or dropped client connections
Managing point-in-time backup snapshots and restore workflows with atomic state verification
screener_signals: Clean Go codebase adhering to standard controller-runtime patterns, status subresource updates, and reconciler interfaces
Comprehensive test suite using envtest and KinD verifying CRD schema validation, reconciliation cycles, and event generation
Anti-fake verification script creating a dynamic cluster CRD with custom replica parameters and asserting controller reconciliation to target state

architecture.data_flow: Users submit Custom Resource manifests (DatabaseCluster) to the Kubernetes API server; the API server stores the resource in etcd and emits an event; the controller-runtime informer detects the event and enqueues a reconciliation request; the reconciler evaluates current child resources (Pods, PVCs, Services, Secrets); if state diverges, the reconciler issues atomic Create/Update/Delete calls; the health monitor periodically checks primary availability; upon failure, the failover engine promotes an eligible replica and updates DNS endpoints; backup controllers trigger point-in-time snapshots according to defined schedules.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: CRD OpenAPI schema validation rejecting invalid manifests; leader election locking ensuring only one active operator instance executes reconciliations.

targets.method: Wall-clock timing from Kubernetes watch event dispatch to successful reconciliation completion
targets.input: 100 synthetic CRD update events across 10 active managed cluster resources in envtest
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Go 1.21+, Kubernetes envtest test suite
targets.minimum_pass: p95 reconciliation execution latency is < 650 milliseconds
targets.target: p95 reconciliation execution latency is < 220 milliseconds
targets.report: Controller-runtime reconciler latency and execution profiling log

targets.metric: Automated Primary Failover Detection & Promotion Time
targets.method: Duration from primary pod termination injection to new primary election, readiness probe pass, and traffic route update
targets.input: 20 simulated primary pod termination and network partition chaos scenarios in KinD cluster
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, KinD (Kubernetes in Docker) local cluster with 3 worker nodes
targets.minimum_pass: Average failover time across 20 trials is < 25.0 seconds with 0 split-brain incidents
targets.target: Average failover time across 20 trials is < 12.0 seconds with 0 split-brain incidents
targets.report: Failover timing and split-brain chaos verification report

targets.metric: CRD Schema Validation Error Rejection Rate

targets.input: 50 invalid CRD manifests (negative replica counts, invalid storage sizes, unparseable cron strings)
targets.environment: Kubernetes API server with custom CRD OpenAPI v3 schema validation enabled

targets.target: 50 of 50 malformed manifests rejected with descriptive admission errors
targets.report: Admission controller and OpenAPI schema validation test log

riskiest_component.name: Split-Brain Primary Election During Ephemeral Network Partitions
riskiest_component.mitigation: Enforce strict lease locks in etcd and double-check replication log offsets before replica promotion.
riskiest_component.fallback: Manual operator intervention mode requiring administrator approval if quorum cannot be validated.
